video.title: AGI, are we there yet..
video.genre: AI explainer and opinion, partly screen-shared

protocol.status: v2 labeler B (rubric v2), independent of A
protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Hook: 'is AGI even possible at all?' Penrose's 1980s claim that understanding is non-algorithmic; today's architectures don't resemble the brain; conclusion (50.0): if we're close to AGI, it doesn't require reproducing human intelligence's mechanism. Opening on the CEO line at 0.1 also works.
Chollet's view: AGI means acquiring skills in novel situations; models are trained for months and frozen at inference, so by his definition we haven't reached AGI (181.6). Short and self-contained.

Hook: Astra hits 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 without learning anything, and the reason is the harness. Harness manages context, memory, execution, error recovery; payoff at 226.3: those are elements of intelligence the model layer alone lacks. Ending at 255.5 (harness outsources hard parts to handwritten code; model+harness shows early signs of AGI) also works as the fuller take; both edges genuinely work. 185.8 adds what ARC-AGI measures.

ANI vs AGI (Tim Urban's framework): general intelligence isn't a pile of narrow skills, so listing tasks AGI can't do is a weak argument; payoff at 397.9: we could have AGI while underperforming narrow AI on some tasks. 406.8 adds the 'transfer and adapt' reason. 341.4 opens on the Tim Urban blog instead.

Hook: Dario calls AGI a marketing term, then ironically offers 'a country of geniuses in a data center, whatever that means'. Turns to: scientific or not, AGI carries huge economic weight; CEOs promise it in 5-10 years; two AI winters came from overpromising; payoff at 483.1: AGI is now an economic narrative, not just a hypothesis. 496.8 adds what it shapes (funding, valuations, data centers, hiring).

also_ok.why: Companies define AGI differently so they'll reach it at different moments, like Jensen saying OpenAI achieved AGI 'using NVIDIA chips. Emphasis on using NVIDIA chips' (joke lands ~512.4, mid-sentence); ends on the sentence's close about managing expectations. Short and opens on 'So'.

negatives.why: LeCun 'LLMs are dead' and his LinkedIn comment 'like this' on screen; framing for the two axes, no payoff here.
Bitter lesson and Boris Cherny's 10-20% figure; opens on 'this certainly brings back to' and leans on the preceding harness argument.
Closing concern that the first AGI may be less capable than existing models; a strong claim resting on the ANI/AGI argument minutes earlier, and cut off by the video's end.
